rationale: Kyodo (Jun 22): North Korea submitted an Asian Games delegation list (~200 athletes, Sports Minister Kim Il Guk as head), so Ri Song Gum (2023 Asiad 49kg champion, 2025 world-record holder) is very likely to compete. Main risks are Japanese entry issues, injury or a top Chinese lifter.

No reports yet of a hunger strike by the four remaining detainees (only a Jun 19 Tunis rally for their release; the June Libya-convoy hunger strike was a different group). Renormalised over the four male detainees, tilted to Naouar, the most prominent, who has a hunger-strike history.

The count reached 70 with Serbia (69th, Jul 16) and Mauritius (70th, Jul 17), the 11th signing of 2026 (~1.7/month). #75 by Sep 27 needs 5 more in ~10 weeks (roughly 40-50% likely), and no upcoming signers have been announced, so the answer stays very diffuse.

Japan Championships (Mar 21): 17-year-old Shin Ohashi won the 200m breaststroke in 2:06.59 (world junior record) ahead of Watanabe (2:08.57); both are on Japan's Asian Games team. China's trial winner Mai Shiting swam 2:09.33 and Qin skipped the 200 at the trials, so Ohashi is a clear favourite in the home-pool final (Sep 24).

The opener is Portugal v Wales (Sep 24, Estadio da Luz). New coach Jorge Jesus (appointed Jul 10, deal to 2030) says he will keep picking Ronaldo, but Ronaldo (41) says the WC was his last and has not decided on his international future. Draw risk is ~20%.

The 9th Cir. Nevada merits appeal (argued Apr 16) and the 4th Cir. Maryland appeal (argued May 7) were still undecided mid-July and may rule before Sep 1. The expedited 6th Cir. Ohio/Tennessee appeal is argued Jul 30 (its motions panel leaned to Ohio), and Kalshi appealed SDNY's Jul 7 pro-New York ruling to the 2nd Cir.

No state settlement or imminent state AG trial against TikTok found as of Jul 21. TikTok keeps settling private bellwethers before trial (R.K.C. settlement in principle Jul 1; Breathitt school district $8M in May), so the forecast stays diffuse.
Nothing new on the 100m. Puripol (9.94 PB) set a 200m national record of 20.03 on Jun 7 and stays the clear favourite, while Japan's champion Tada won nationals in only 10.17.

JESU lists Japan's Puyo Puyo candidate 'Yuki' under his legal name Yuki Kurihara (born 2015, Tokyo Verdy esports). He won the GigaCrysta Grand Prix Final and the Mar 22 selection; the final is Sep 26 and Japanese players dominate the title.

Spain are the new world champions (beat Argentina 1-0 AET, Jul 19) and England finished third (beat France 6-4). England's Wembley home edge roughly offsets Spain's higher rating; the fixture is listed for Sat Sep 26.

Antonelli won the Belgian GP on Jul 19, his 6th win in 10 races, and leads the title race. Mercedes have 8 wins, Ferrari 2 (Hamilton, Leclerc) and Verstappen has race pace. Baku's long straight suits Mercedes' straight-line speed.

Reports on Jul 16-17 said selectors had dropped Rohit from 2027 plans; the BCCI denied them and Rohit hit a century at Lord's (Jul 19), saying he wants to keep representing India. Gill (Jul 13) says Kohli is in the 2027 plans. Nobody has yet called 2027 his last.

Final concepts from Munich, KölnRheinRuhr and Berlin (Hamburg withdrew after its May 31 referendum) are being evaluated in Jun-Sep, with the vote at the DOSB extraordinary assembly in Baden-Baden on Sep 26. No evaluation leak yet; Munich (66.4% referendum, 1972 legacy) stays the favourite.
It is the off-season and there are no new results. Sivasangari (world ~No. 5, 8-1 against Watanabe) stays the favourite, trimmed slightly for knockout variance and Watanabe's home crowd in Japan.

The FAI confirmed Israel's Sep 27 'home' game will be at a neutral venue, the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen, Hungary. FAI delegates voted 75-32 on Jul 8 to fulfil the fixtures, so there's no forfeit risk and little home edge for Israel; neither side played at the WC.
It is the off-season and nothing new turned up. Ng Eain Yow (2023 champion) stays a modest favourite in an open field.

No new revocations beyond the precedents (Norway Aug 2024, Australia Aug 2025). Spain dropped because it runs a Jerusalem consulate, not a Ramallah office. Ireland and the Netherlands are moving national settlement-trade bans (Jul 13), likely triggers for retaliation before Israel's October election.

Sindhu won the Japan Open (Super 750) on Jul 19, beating Akane Yamaguchi 21-17 21-17 for her first title in almost two years, after a SF and several QFs this season. Mass shifted toward SF/Final, but a likely QF against An Se-young or a top Chinese/Japanese seed caps her.

France (Zidane takes over Sep 1) play both matchday 1-2 games away, at Türkiye Sep 25 and Belgium Sep 28. Italy missed a third straight WC, Belgium reached the WC QF and Türkiye host both their games. A Poisson simulation gives France ~0.34-0.42.

Florida's Jun 1 suit seeks injunctions and was removed on Jul 2 to federal court (Judge Cannon), with OpenAI's response due Aug 24, so a Florida injunction motion in September is plausible. No other state AG suit against OpenAI has been reported.

Pathirage (92.62 world lead, Rome Jun 4) is the CWG favourite. Arshad is fit, planned a Swiss DL start and defends his CWG title on Aug 1. India's Rohit Yadav threw 87.05 on Jun 28 (world No. 2), while Neeraj's SB is 85.69 after a back injury.

Hespress, Le360 and Maroc Hebdo (Jul 21) report that Budget Minister and FRMF president Fouzi Lekjaa will join PAM's political bureau and run in Berkane, to be announced at PAM's Jul 25 council; observers frame it as a bid for head of government. Analysts (Le Matin, Jul 13) still see RNI under Chaouki leading, with Istiqlal the main challenger; vote Sep 23.

The draw is on Jul 23, so the bracket is unknown. Korea named a strong squad on Jul 9 (three WC players as overage picks plus Bae Jun-ho, nine Europe-based) chasing a fourth straight gold, and Japan beat China 4-0 in January's U23 Asian Cup final. Re-weight once the draw is made.
